source.title: Truth Neurons
source.authors: Hao-Hang Li; Yupeng Cao; Yang-Yang Yu; J. Suchow; Zi-Ning Zhu

record.tranche_reason: The study uses neuron-level attribution and suppression to investigate truthfulness, but does not test whether most neuron poles have a single interpretable job or test the explanation claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports causal effects of suppressing attribution-identified truth neurons. These results concern neuron-level analysis, but measure truthfulness-task performance rather than neuron-job counts, explanations tested on held-out activations, or the specific explanation properties in V1–V7. The suppression and benchmark results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study selects neurons by integrated-gradient attribution and zero-ablates them to show effects on truthfulness benchmarks. It never explains neurons from activating examples, never scores explanations by simulation, and never counts neuron poles by job. Its results therefore bear on no version (V1–V7). Using neuron-level attribution as a tool does not test whether neurons are already clean.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that truth neurons exist across models and encode truthfulness in a subject- and category-agnostic way. They report that suppressing them degrades TruthfulQA and, except Qwen on MMLU, TriviaQA/MMLU accuracy. They also report that the neurons' layer distribution, mid layers plus some late layers, matches prior truth-geometry findings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses integrated-gradient neuron attribution, filtering, statistical tests, and activation suppression to study truthfulness; it does not test natural-language neuron explanations or the pole/job proportions in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The adaptive attribution threshold was manually tuned separately for each model; the paper warns that thresholds that are too high can yield negligible effects and thresholds that are too low can impair instruction-following.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing attribution-selected 'truth neurons' (35–655 per model) lowered binary TruthfulQA accuracy in all six models. Equal-count random-neuron ablation left accuracy near baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small set of attribution-selected MLP/attention neurons causally supports truthful answer selection in instruct LLMs, beyond random-ablation control.

fits_no_version.finding: Neurons selected on TruthfulQA mostly also lowered TriviaQA and MMLU accuracy. The size of the drop varied widely (0.5 to 22.7 points), and Qwen2.5-3B on MMLU rose slightly. No random-ablation control was run for these datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Truth neurons found on one dataset transfer their ablation effect to other factual QA benchmarks, unevenly across models.

fits_no_version.finding: Truth neurons cluster in middle layers, with secondary concentrations in later layers (Figure 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attribution-identified truthfulness neurons concentrate in middle-to-late layers.

record.problems: The adaptive thresholds were manually tuned per model. The paper notes that overly low thresholds can include unrelated neurons and impair instruction-following. Table 2 reports no uncertainty estimates, and the category-specific comparison is described without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows were omitted. The category-specific statements are noted under fits_no_version but not entered as rows because the text gives no separate numerical values for the categories.

untested.parts: Share of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one job, two related jobs, or not understood.
Neuron-job shares across other models, MoE architectures, and trillion-parameter scale.
Reinterpretation of canonical polysemantic vision neurons; recursive generalization.
Effect of architecture, regularization and tools on the share of interpretable neurons.
Neuron-based attribution graphs explaining behaviour without a replacement model.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict where neurons fire.

record.verdict_notes: The study bears on no version, so no verdicts are given. Caveats for the fits_no_version findings: the adaptive threshold was tuned per model until a noticeable drop appeared (Qwen t=1%, others 10–25%), which biases toward finding effects. Tables 2 has no random-neuron control or uncertainty. MMLU drops (e.g., OLMo-7B 50.81→28.13) may reflect general capability damage rather than truth-specific encoding.

versions.untested_parts: The share of neuron poles with one job, two related jobs, or jobs not yet understood.
Shares across models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or trillion-parameter scales.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car interpretation and recursive generalization.
Effects of architecture, regularization, and tool quality on neuron interpretability, including the InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
Whether attribution graphs from a large model's own neurons explain behavior without a trained replacement model or reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fitting activating examples fail to predict other activations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
